messages:
cheng: Heads-up: after the kernel-selector v2 rollout we see a regression on AMD nodes for long sequences (>2048). Spike in p95 and a bunch of kernel fallbacks in the logs.

cheng: Log snippet:
```
[WARN] kernel_selector: no optimized kernel for arch=gfx1030 seq_len=4096 model=gpt-medium -> falling back to generic_attention_fwd
[INFO] runtime: selected kernel=generic_attention_fwd (estimated flops 12.1G)
```

maria: Oof. Are autotune traces available? Is KV cache warm or cold when this happens?

cheng: I grabbed an autotune dump and a quick rdw-profile run. KV cache was warm (we were streaming tokens). Profile cmd: `rdw-profile --backend=rocm --model=gpt-medium --seq=4096 --iters=20`. Results copied below.

devon: Paste of the small autotune CSV (trimmed):
```
arch,gfx,seq,graph_kern,duration_ms
gfx1030,roc,512,optim_fmha,1.9
gfx1030,roc,1024,optim_fmha,4.2
gfx1030,roc,2048,optim_fmha,9.1
gfx1030,roc,4096,generic_attention_fwd,36.8
gfx1030,roc,8192,generic_attention_fwd,78.5
```

devon: You can see the selector switches to the generic kernel at 4096; generic is ~4x slower relative to expected trend. Perf counters show memory-bound stalls and large global loads for KV slices.

lucas: Does the kernel registry contain any seq-length-aware optimized path for gfx1030? I remember a newer patch that added a tiled-fmha for gfx10+ but it didn’t ship to the package on the AMD nodes. Might be a packaging availability gap.

cheng: Yeah — the optimized tiled kernel (optim_fmha_v2) exists in the repo but our runtime only registers it when the driver/lib version >= ROCm-5.6. Our AMD pool still has 5.5. So kernel_selector thinks it’s unavailable and falls back.

maria: Two short-term options:
- Update node images to ROCm-5.6+ (rolling upgrade, risk: infra work).
- Add conditional routing so long-seq requests go to Dedicated CUDA pool for affected customers until infra is patched.

lucas: Proposed routing rule (console config snippet):
```
{
  "match": ["model:gpt-medium","seq_len:>2048","pool:rocm"],
  "action": "route",
  "target": "pool:dedicated-cuda-canary",
  "reason": "rocm_missing_optim_kernel_gfx1030"
}
```

devon: Alternative quick fix: teach kernel-selector to prefer a slower but available tiled kernel for 4096 (less memory pressure) instead of full generic_attention_fwd. That requires a tiny selector patch (low risk) and would avoid cross-pool routing.

infra-bot: CI: amd-node-image-upgrade pipeline failed on staging (missing kernel modules), build #3421. :warning:

cheng: Thanks. I’ll open a patch to selector to add the intermediate tile as a fallback and also raise an infra ticket for ROCm image updates. Can someone run a canary with the selector patch?

maria: I can run canary on the small customer group (non-prod) later today. Will post perf numbers. :thumbsup:

devon: Quick numbers from local canary w/ selector patch (toy run):
- seq 4096 p50: 220ms -> 180ms (selector patch)
- seq 4096 p95: 1.2s -> 0.45s (selector patch)
- baseline 1024 unchanged

lucas: Good improvement. Still want infra to upgrade ROCm so the real optim_v2 can be used. Also consider adding an autotune metric alert when selector falls back more than X% to generic kernels for a model+arch pair.

sre-oncall: Please file an incident for the customer-impact routing plan so we can track SLA changes.

cheng: Will file an incident and link this thread. TO-DOs: 1) dev patch to selector fallback (devon), 2) infra ticket for ROCm upgrade (cheng+infra), 3) routing rule if patch insufficient (lucas/maria), 4) add autotune fallback alert (product/observability).

maria: Ping me when patch is in canary, I’ll run longer perf runs and KV-warm/cold tests.

cheng: thanks all. keeping this thread as the source for the incident notes.
